alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: Turtle Creek valley
alerts.text: The line drops into the Turtle Creek valley at East Pittsburgh, past the old Westinghouse Electric works. Huge concrete arches are coming up overhead.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ George Westinghouse Bridge
alerts.text: Look up: the 1932 concrete-arch bridge carrying US 30 soars high over the valley and the tracks.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Wilmerding: the Westinghouse 'Castle'
alerts.text: Watch for the turreted brick Westinghouse Air Brake office building, the castle of this old company town, right by the tracks.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Pitcairn yard
alerts.text: This is Norfolk Southern's Pitcairn yard. Look for long rows of freight cars, containers and locomotives.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Section: Brush Creek valley
alerts.text: Past Trafford the line climbs the wooded Brush Creek valley toward Manor and Jeannette, with small towns and hillside farms.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Jeannette, the Glass City
alerts.text: Jeannette grew around huge glass works. Look for old factory sites and the brick town beside the line.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Greensburg: courthouse dome
alerts.text: Look RIGHT for the tall dome of the Westmoreland County Courthouse above town. Greensburg's restored 1912 station is next to the tracks.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Latrobe
alerts.text: Latrobe is the hometown of Fred Rogers and Arnold Palmer, and where the banana split was invented. Rolling farmland follows, then the ridges.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Derry
alerts.text: Derry is an old Pennsylvania Railroad yard town. The flatlands end soon: the line heads for the Conemaugh River and the first mountain gap.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Packsaddle Gap
alerts.text: The line follows the Conemaugh River where it cuts through Chestnut Ridge. Watch the steep wooded walls rise on both sides. This is the first of two big gaps.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ New Florence: between the ridges
alerts.text: This is an open valley between Chestnut Ridge, behind you, and Laurel Ridge, ahead. The deeper Conemaugh Gap starts after Seward.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Section: Conemaugh Gap
alerts.text: The Conemaugh Gap is the deep gorge the river carved through Laurel Ridge, well over 1,000 ft deep. Watch both sides for the next ~10 miles into Johnstown.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Conemaugh Gap: heart of the gorge
alerts.text: You're in the deepest part of the gorge now. Look up at the ridgetops towering over the river.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Johnstown: Stone Bridge & Incline
alerts.text: The train crosses the 1888 Stone Bridge, where debris from the 1889 Johnstown Flood piled up. Look RIGHT for the Inclined Plane climbing the steep hillside above the city.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: climb up the Little Conemaugh
alerts.text: East of Johnstown the line climbs along the Little Conemaugh River through Mineral Point and South Fork, with the valley narrowing and wooded slopes.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ South Fork: 1889 flood history
alerts.text: The South Fork Dam stood just up the valley from here. Its failure in 1889 sent the flood that destroyed Johnstown. The memorial site is out of view.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Lilly
alerts.text: You're near the top of the climb up the Allegheny Front. Cresson and the summit tunnel are ahead.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Cresson: near the summit
alerts.text: This is high Allegheny country near the summit of the old Pennsylvania Railroad main line. Gallitzin's tunnel is next, then Horseshoe Curve.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Gallitzin: Allegheny Tunnel
alerts.text: The Allegheny Tunnel at Gallitzin (3,600 ft) is ahead, with Gallitzin Tunnels Park beside the tracks. GPS cuts out inside. Get ready for Horseshoe Curve after it.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Horseshoe Curve: get to a window
alerts.text: Horseshoe Curve is coming up on the descent. Get to a window now. On the bend you can often see the front or back of your own train.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Horseshoe Curve
alerts.text: You're on the 1854 Horseshoe Curve now. Look RIGHT, to the inside of the bend, for the park, the reservoirs below, and the rest of your train curving around.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: descent into Altoona
alerts.text: The line drops the rest of the way into Altoona, the Pennsylvania Railroad's old shop city. Rail yards start soon.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Altoona: station & railroad museum
alerts.text: Altoona station. The Railroaders Memorial Museum is beside the tracks on the RIGHT.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Juniata locomotive shops
alerts.text: Look LEFT for the giant Juniata shops, among the largest locomotive repair shops in North America. You may spot locomotives parked outside.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ East Altoona yards
alerts.text: The last of the Altoona yards. The Little Juniata gorge begins at Tyrone.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Little Juniata gorge
alerts.text: From Tyrone the line winds down the Little Juniata gorge, with repeated river crossings, close wooded ridges and a tunnel. It's scenic all the way to Petersburg.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Little Juniata: Birmingham
alerts.text: Watch the river crossings and folded ridges around Birmingham.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Little Juniata: river crossings
alerts.text: This is a run of crossings over the Little Juniata. Look down at the river and at the stone-arch bridge piers.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Spruce Creek tunnel
alerts.text: The line tunnels through a spur of Tussey Mountain here. GPS may drop out briefly.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Little Juniata: Barree
alerts.text: Big river bends and steep wooded slopes around Barree.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Petersburg: end of the gorge
alerts.text: The Little Juniata joins the Juniata near here. Huntingdon is next, then Jacks Narrows.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Huntingdon
alerts.text: Huntingdon station and riverside town. Jacks Narrows begins after Mapleton, about 15 minutes ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Jacks Narrows
alerts.text: At Mapleton the line enters Jacks Narrows, a water gap through Jacks Mountain. Watch the river and the mountain walls closing in.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Jacks Narrows: Thousand Steps
alerts.text: Look LEFT up the steep quarried face of Jacks Mountain. The Thousand Steps, built by quarry workers, climb it, though trees can hide them.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Mount Union
alerts.text: This is the east end of Jacks Narrows. Mount Union was once a silica-brick capital. The Juniata valley continues to Lewistown.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Lewistown: 1849 depot
alerts.text: Watch for the historic 1849 depot at Lewistown, one of the oldest surviving Pennsylvania Railroad stations. The Lewistown Narrows are right after it.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Lewistown Narrows
alerts.text: In the Lewistown Narrows, the Juniata squeezes between steep Blue and Shade Mountain ridges. Keep watching for the next ~10 miles.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Lewistown Narrows: Hawstone
alerts.text: You're deep in the narrows at Hawstone, where the river, highway and railroad share the gorge.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Lewistown Narrows: Denholm bend
alerts.text: Watch the big river bend with the ridges around it. Remains of the old canal corridor are across the river.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ End of the narrows
alerts.text: The valley widens again. The Juniata keeps winding toward the Susquehanna at Duncannon.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Susquehanna River
alerts.text: Here the Juniata joins the wide Susquehanna. The Appalachian Trail crosses on the Clarks Ferry Bridge. Next comes the river run to Harrisburg, with two top sights.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Statue of Liberty (Dauphin Narrows)
alerts.text: Look LEFT, out in the river: a 25-ft Statue of Liberty replica stands on an old bridge pier in the Susquehanna.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Rockville Bridge
alerts.text: The train crosses the Rockville Bridge (1902), the world's longest stone-arch railroad bridge, with 48 arches. Look upstream (LEFT) toward the mountain gap.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Harrisburg
alerts.text: Harrisburg: the train swaps diesel for electric power here, so expect a longer stop. Look RIGHT for the Capitol dome as you arrive. Fast electrified running follows.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Three Mile Island
alerts.text: Look RIGHT across the fields and river for the Three Mile Island cooling towers. They may show through gaps in the trees.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Lancaster
alerts.text: This is Lancaster's grand 1929 station. Pennsylvania Dutch farm country starts right after.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Amish farmland
alerts.text: This is Lancaster County farm country. Watch for Amish farms, horse-drawn buggies, big barns and windmills between here and Gap.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Leaman Place
alerts.text: This is the junction for the Strasburg Rail Road, a steam tourist line. Farmland continues on both sides.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Gap
alerts.text: At Gap the line tops the grade out of Lancaster County. Keep watching for buggies on the back roads.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Parkesburg
alerts.text: Here the farmland gives way to Chester County hills and old iron and steel towns.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Coatesville: Brandywine & steel mill
alerts.text: The line crosses high over the West Branch Brandywine. Look down at the long steel mill that grew from Lukens Steel, one of America's oldest.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: Philadelphia Main Line
alerts.text: From Paoli the train runs down the historic Main Line, past leafy suburbs, stone stations and college towns, into Philadelphia.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Bryn Mawr
alerts.text: This is a classic Main Line stone station and suburb. Villanova and Haverford are just up and down the line.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Philadelphia skyline
alerts.text: Look RIGHT for the Center City skyline as the train swings toward the Schuylkill River and 30th Street.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ 30th Street Station
alerts.text: This is Philadelphia's grand 1933 30th Street Station. The train reverses here during a long stop, then heads north up the Northeast Corridor.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Schuylkill River crossing
alerts.text: The train crosses the Schuylkill River. Look downriver (RIGHT) toward the Art Museum and Boathouse Row area.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Delaware River: 'Trenton Makes'
alerts.text: The train crosses the Delaware into New Jersey. Look LEFT for the 'TRENTON MAKES THE WORLD TAKES' sign on the road bridge next to you.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Trenton
alerts.text: This is Trenton, New Jersey's capital. The gold State House dome may show LEFT.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Princeton Junction
alerts.text: Princeton Junction, where the little two-mile 'Dinky' shuttle branches off to Princeton University.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ New Brunswick & Raritan River
alerts.text: Right after New Brunswick station (Rutgers) the train crosses the Raritan River on a long bridge. Look down the river.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Newark Airport
alerts.text: Look RIGHT for Newark Liberty Airport, with jets taking off and landing and the AirTrain monorail.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Newark Penn & Passaic River
alerts.text: Newark Penn Station. Right after it, the train crosses the Passaic River on the Dock Bridge lift span. The Manhattan skyline comes next.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Section: Manhattan skyline
alerts.text: Crossing the Meadowlands marshes. Look RIGHT for the Manhattan skyline, including the Empire State Building and One World Trade Center.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Portal Bridge (Hackensack River)
alerts.text: The train crosses the Hackensack River, where the old 1910 Portal swing bridge is being replaced by the new Portal North Bridge.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Secaucus: last skyline view
alerts.text: Last skyline look (RIGHT) before the train dives under the Palisades and the Hudson River into New York Penn Station. GPS ends in the tunnel.
